application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A tiny TypeScript HTTP client library (the unjs 'ofetch' project) that wraps the Fetch API with automatic JSON handling, baseURL/query composition, response-type detection, retries, timeouts, lifecycle hooks, and normalized FetchError objects.
application.purpose: Provide a unified, ergonomic '$fetch' / 'ofetch' function for making HTTP requests across runtimes (Node, browsers, etc.) with smart defaults and rich error/context information.

domains.name: HTTP Fetch Core
domains.description: Factory and request pipeline: option resolution, request preparation, execution via native fetch, response parsing, and error/retry handling.

domains.name: Error Normalization
domains.description: Creation of a standardized FetchError carrying request, options, response, parsed data, and HTTP status information.

domains.name: URL & Query Composition
domains.description: Joining baseURL with request paths and serializing query parameters (including arrays, objects, and undefined values).

domains.name: Request Body Serialization
domains.description: Auto-detection and JSON/form-urlencoded serialization of request bodies; Content-Type and Accept header defaults; streaming body support.

domains.name: Response Parsing
domains.description: Content-type-based detection of response type (json, text, blob, stream) and safe JSON parsing via 'destr'.

domains.name: Lifecycle Hooks
domains.description: User-invoked onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError callbacks receiving a FetchContext.

domains.name: Retry & Timeout Policies
domains.description: Configurable retries, retry delays, retryable status codes, and request timeouts via AbortSignal.

domains.name: Testing & Tooling
domains.description: Vitest-based integration tests against a local h3 server, plus a manual playground script.

terminology.meaning: The library's public fetch function instance with an enhanced API (raw, native, create).
Normalized error thrown on request failure or HTTP error status; exposes request, options, response, data, status, statusCode, statusText, statusMessage.
Per-request state object holding request, resolved options, response, and error; passed to hooks and error creation.
User callback invoked at lifecycle points: onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError; may be a single function or an array.
HTTP methods that carry a body (PATCH, POST, PUT, DELETE); affects default retry count (0 for payload methods vs 1 otherwise).
Desired parsed response shape: json, text, blob, arrayBuffer, or stream.
HTTP status codes considered retryable; defaults to 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504.
Prefix prepended to relative request paths when not already present.
URL query parameters; 'params' is a deprecated alias for 'query'; merged from defaults and per-call options.
External safe-JSON parser used instead of JSON.parse for response bodies (unless parseResponse is provided).
Status codes (101, 204, 205, 304) whose responses are treated as having no body.
Option to resolve (rather than throw) on HTTP error statuses (400-599).

entityAnnotations.businessMeaning: Core factory producing a '$fetch' client instance. Defines the full request pipeline: resolve options, run onRequest hooks, apply baseURL/query, serialize JSON bodies, set timeout signal, call native fetch, parse response per detected/declared responseType, run onResponse hooks, and route error statuses to onError. Also exposes '.raw' (full response), '.native' (bypass), and '.create' (new instance with merged defaults - hence the recursive CALLS edge to itself).

Internal error-and-retry handler of a fetch instance. Detects user aborts (no auto-retry), computes retry counts (payload methods default to 0 retries, others 1), waits retryDelay, retries via the raw fetch path on retryable status codes, otherwise throws a normalized FetchError.

Builds a FetchError with a formatted message ('[METHOD] "url": status statusText'), original error as cause, and lazily-bound getters for request, options, response, data, status, statusCode, statusText, and statusMessage.
Merges per-call options with instance defaults: combines headers (via mergeHeaders) and consolidates query/params from both sources into one query object.
Creates a Headers object from default headers, then overlays per-call/request headers on top; internal helper (not exported).
Executes one hook or an array of hooks sequentially, awaiting each with the FetchContext.
Returns true for PATCH, POST, PUT, DELETE (case-insensitive); used for body handling and default retry policy.
Detects whether a request body can be auto-serialized to JSON (primitives, arrays, plain objects, toJSON); excludes FormData, URLSearchParams, buffers, and streams.
Infers how to parse a response from its Content-Type: JSON patterns -> json, text/event-stream -> stream (SSE), text-like types -> text, otherwise blob; empty header defaults to json.
Prepends the configured baseURL to a request path unless the path already starts with it.
Joins a base URL and path ensuring exactly one separating slash.
Strips a trailing slash from a path; internal helper used by withBase.

Appends or merges query parameters into a URL: sets/overwrites existing keys when no '?' present logic differs - merges into existing search params when '?' exists, omits undefined values, expands arrays into repeated keys, and JSON-serializes object values.
Converts a single query value to string form: null -> empty string, numbers/booleans via String(), objects via JSON.stringify.
Demo of typed responses: fetches the ofetch repo metadata from ungh.cc (https://ungh.cc/repos/unjs/ofetch) with a typed generic and prints its star count.
Test helper that aborts an in-flight request (with retry enabled) and asserts the request rejects with an 'aborted' error, verifying user aborts are not auto-retried.
Manual playground script that fetches http://httpstat.us/500 to observe error/retry behavior; exits with code 1 on error.

applicationFacts: Public API is exported from src/index.ts: 'ofetch' and its alias '$fetch', both created via createFetch with a patchable reference to globalThis.fetch (allows runtime fetch patching).
createFetch defines a nested raw implementation ($fetchRaw) and a convenience wrapper returning parsed data; these closures are not separate graph entities.
Default retry behavior: 1 retry for non-payload methods, 0 for PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE; retries only on retryStatusCodes (408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504).
User-initiated aborts (AbortError without timeout) are never auto-retried; timeouts use AbortSignal.timeout combined with any user signal via AbortSignal.any.

JSON-serializable bodies are auto-stringified; Content-Type and Accept default to application/json unless already set; form-urlencoded bodies use URLSearchParams; ReadableStream/Node stream bodies get duplex 'half' automatically.
JSON responses are parsed with 'destr' (safe JSON) unless a custom parseResponse is provided; responseType can be forced to json, text, blob, arrayBuffer, or stream.
HTTP statuses 400-599 throw FetchError unless ignoreResponseError is set; null-body statuses (101, 204, 205, 304) and HEAD requests skip body parsing.
Hooks (onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError) accept a single function or an array and are awaited sequentially; hook errors propagate to the caller.
$fetch.create builds derived instances with deep-merged defaults (query, params, headers merged from global defaults, custom defaults, and per-create options).

Integration tests (test/index.test.ts) run against a local h3 server with routes like /ok, /echo, /post, /binary, /403, /408, /204, /timeout, exercising parsing, retries, timeouts, aborts, hooks, and header merging.

src/base.ts re-exports fetch and error modules; src/types.ts defines the public type surface ($Fetch, FetchOptions, FetchContext, FetchError interface, ResponseType map) but contains no captured function entities.
